def: A row that does not fit the pattern of the rest of the data, judged against a model of normal behaviour.
Deciding whether new rows resemble a training set believed to be clean, as opposed to finding outliers within unlabelled data.
The effect by which anomalies inflate the statistics used to detect them, so that none of them looks extreme.
The median of the absolute differences from the median, a spread measure that outliers barely affect.
A robust z-score that replaces the mean and standard deviation with the median and the MAD, usually flagged above 3.5.
A rule that flags values beyond 1.5 interquartile ranges outside the first or third quartile.
Distance from the mean measured in units of the data's own covariance, so points off the main correlation ridge count as far away.
A score comparing a point's local density with the density of its neighbours, near 1 for normal points and well above 1 for local anomalies.
An ensemble of random trees that scores a row by how few random cuts are needed to isolate it, so anomalies get short paths.
The number of splits needed to isolate a point in a random tree, averaged over trees to give an isolation score.
Overlooking how rare an event is, so that a small false-positive rate produces far more false alarms than true alerts.
A group of rows that is unusual together even though each member looks ordinary.
